LanguageData.SCP_ContactReplyText:
This is O5-7. You may call me The Green.

We received your message about the Black Statue. To justify assistance to your settlement, you must demonstrate that you can maintain containment of anomalous objects.

Please take SCP-650 into temporary custody: move the statue to a post, prepare a chamber and arrange observation. Accumulate 24 hours of proper containment, then submit confirmation through the terminal. The Foundation will provide 10 medicine, 10 components and 5 advanced components as initial assistance.

Confirm your agreement. The object at the post will be registered automatically.

The statue at a post is detected automatically. A violation or removal pauses the timer until conditions are restored.\n\nAfter a full day, submit confirmation through a powered terminal to receive 10 medicine, 10 components and 5 advanced components. One reward, with no failure deadline. The terminal need not stay powered during containment.

LanguageData.SCP_055Observed: Clearance level 1.\n\nSCP-055 is Keter: a self-keeping secret. Information about its appearance, nature, behavior and origin suppresses itself.
LanguageData.SCP_055Partial:
Clearance level 2.

SCP-055 is an antimeme. Information about it leaves human memory soon after observation.

The Foundation does not know how, when or by whom it was acquired. The object is neither invisible nor impossible to describe: personnel can observe it and create notes, sketches, photographs and recordings. Soon afterward they lose focus, interest and memory of what they recorded. Camera operators finish a shift exhausted and unable to recall the preceding hours. The author and purpose of the chamber procedures are unknown, and Site-19 personnel fail to remember that SCP-055 exists despite easy access to its chamber. These facts are periodically rediscovered, cause brief alarm and are then forgotten again. A large body of scientific data exists, but cannot be studied.
LanguageData.SCP_055Documented:
Clearance level 3.

SCP-055 may present a substantial physical threat and may already have caused hundreds of deaths without leaving a usable memory. It is certainly a memetic and mental threat, which is the basis for its Keter classification.

The research team confirmed that negative facts persist better than positive ones. Personnel can repeatedly deduce that SCP-055 exists and that it is not a sphere, while remaining unable to remember the object itself.

Without renewed research, detailed information decays after twenty hours and the dossier returns to clearance level 1.
LanguageData.SCP_055Interview:
Excerpt from a personnel debrief:

{0}: I am going to ask you some questions about fifty-five.

{1}: Fifty-what?

{0}: SCP-055. The object you just examined.

{1}: I do not understand. I do not think we even have a fifty-five.

{0}: Then tell me what you did for the last two hours.

{1}: I… do not know.

{0}: Do you remember agreeing that it was not spherical?

{1}: Right! It was not round. Object fifty-five was not round.

{0}: Do you remember it now?

{1}: Not exactly. Something is there, something that cannot be remembered, and it is not spherical.

{0}: What is not spherical?

{1}: Object fifty-five.

{0}: Object what?

{1}: Do you remember agreeing that something was not spherical?

{0}: Right.

LanguageData.SCP_MonitorGuideBody:
Remote observation replaces personnel standing near an SCP only while the complete chain works:
1. Build and power a camera inside the containment chamber. It must be mounted on a wall, remain in the same room, stay within 12 cells and have a clear view. Rotation is visual and does not change coverage. 2. Every eligible object appears at the console automatically as soon as it stands on its bound post. There is no manual object selection. 3. Assign an operator in “Shifts”, or order a colonist to operate the console. The operator counts only after actually reaching the console interaction cell. 4. Keep the camera and console powered. When both checks pass, the operator replaces the required observers at the post.
A brief containment failure does not remove an object from the console while it remains on its post. The console inspection panel shows separate camera and operator checks. Once every containment requirement is met, assigned staff restore containment automatically. Physical observers beside the SCP remain a valid fallback.

LanguageData.SCP_882FinalReportBody:
FINAL PROTOCOL · SCP-882
Status: the object remains contained in its reservoir at the colony.
Basis: site defense, object analysis, and O5-7 Green's personal inspection.

The Council orders SCP-882 to remain in place. Transporting the object or attempting to assemble the mechanism is unauthorized. The original coordinates of the answering signal remain sealed; the Church of the Broken God is denied access to the measurements. The colony will continue containment and research under existing protocols.

The operation to defend the object is complete. The source of the answering signal remains a separate classified case.

The transponder recovered from the deserted relay contains a repeating packet from the SCP-882 defense recordings. The researcher identified the next hop: a Church of the Broken God assembly cache. Its manifest lists a sealed SCP-217 sample and components linked to SCP-629. After the 1943 assembly, this combination warrants immediate action. This does not prove that the Church sent the original signal.

O5-7 authorized a raid on the cache. SCP-882 containment protocol remains unchanged.

LanguageData.SCP_RoutingLogArchiveBody:
SERVICE LOG · FOUNDATION CLOSED CHANNEL
The Church-made plate attached to SCP-629's parts identified a former routing node. The expedition recovered its physical log. The first record of the SCP-882 signal appeared here before the Church received its copy. The packet entered through a closed Foundation channel, but the log preserves only a service key number; the sender's name was removed before this hop.

Conclusion: the Church did not originate the signal. Someone used Foundation infrastructure or a stolen key. O5-7 has requested the original key registry. No specific employee can be accused from this log alone.
LanguageData.SCP_OuroborosFinalLetter: O5-7 has checked the service key against the original registry. The complete Ouroboros case and the conclusion on the SCP-882 signal are available in the Foundation archive. Foundation trust: +{0}. The investigation is complete.
LanguageData.SCP_OuroborosFinalOutgoing: We recovered the physical routing log. Please compare its key number with the original registry, release the complete 001 case and close the investigation into the SCP-882 signal.
LanguageData.SCP_OuroborosFinalReply: The comparison is complete. The key belonged to an old automated Project 001 accounting line, not a current employee. Its emergency notice about SCP-882 went through a channel believed to be closed. The Church intercepted a copy; the Chaos Insurgency exploited the leak. We have isolated the line and revoked its key. A complete summary of Ouroboros's four parts is in your archive. SCP-882 remains in your custody. You have done enough. — O5-7 “Green”
LanguageData.SCP_OuroborosFinalBody:
CASE 001 · OUROBOROS · COMPLETE SUMMARY
Released by O5-7 after recovery of the routing log. These are four connected 001 files, not one creature. The conclusion about your colony appears at the end.

I. THE CHILDREN
In the 1920s, a Foundation research group made a weapon from nine children, able to destroy targets at immense range. The project was hidden under the 001 designation. Its leader, the future O5-1, used that power against the Administrator and disappeared. A new Overseer Council followed, while some fugitives became the core of the future Chaos Insurgency. The children remained alive: a reminder of the cost the Foundation called protection.

II. THE BROKEN GOD
In 1942–1943, the Church of the Broken God assembled a vast mechanical entity from scattered anomalous parts. These included SCP-217, SCP-882 and some components of SCP-629. It absorbed metal and sought more parts. The Allied Occult Initiative, predecessor of the Global Occult Coalition, helped stop it. The assembly broke apart: active components went to Foundation sites, while the inactive core remained elsewhere. Finding parts in the Church's present cache justified the Council's alarm, but did not prove a second assembly was complete.

III. ATONEMENT
Decades later, the Foundation faced another 001: an intelligent gravitational singularity tied to researcher Calvin Desmet. It claimed that colliding realities would destroy every world and offered to save one by annihilating all the others. The Council debated that price; O5-7 opposed it. The offer was a deception. Releasing the entity would have endangered the very world that trusted it. The case remained classified and contained.

IV. THE WAY IT ENDS
The Chaos Insurgency declared war on the Overseer Council. Its operation reached the Overseers, but destroying the old leadership did not destroy the institution: the victor took the place he had fought and formed a new Council. History returned to its starting point. Ouroboros names this cycle: power, fear, secrecy and the promise to save the world keep producing decisions from which it must then be saved.

SCP-882 CONCLUSION · COLONY EVENTS
The log, the cache cipher and the original key registry match. In this mod's story, a forgotten automated Project 001 accounting line emitted the signal: it flagged SCP-882 as a possible component of another assembly and sent an emergency notice. Its old channel was no longer closed to outsiders. The Church received a copy after transmission; the Chaos Insurgency used the leak to attack. This is no evidence that O5-7 or present staff betrayed the colony. The Council isolated the line and revoked the key. The colony disrupted the Church's collection, kept SCP-882 contained and closed the investigation. No further expeditions are required.

The relay led the team to a guarded Church of the Broken God outpost. A sealed SCP-217 sample, components linked to SCP-629 and a cipher log were found. The team copied the log and brought both containers home. The Church cannot repeat the 1943 assembly with this shipment. Keep the cargos sealed.

The log confirms that the Church received a copy of the SCP-882 signal, but does not identify the original sender. O5-7 authorized use of the technical notes in fusor research. LanguageData.SCP_ChurchCacheBody:
FIELD REPORT · CHURCH CIPHER CACHE
The relay record led the team to a small Church of the Broken God outpost. Its cipher core held the next transmission hop and technical notes on a power circuit. The Church monitored the signal after the SCP-882 attack, but the surviving packets do not prove it sent the original impulse.

O5-7 authorized use of the notes in fusor research. The Foundation awarded trust and transferred SCP-458 from its canteen as a safe staff object. The original sender remains unknown. Send the copied cipher through an online terminal for comparison with the sealed Foundation archive.

LanguageData.SCP_ChurchResolutionMessage: Comparison complete. The Church was an intermediate recipient. The original packet used a sealed Foundation channel format, but that does not prove a staff member sent it. The next lead is a missing routing log. Until then, contain SCP-882 and keep the data within the colony.
LanguageData.SCP_ChurchResolutionBody:
SEALED COMPARISON · O5-7 RESPONSE
The cache cipher confirms that the Church received a copy after the signal passed through the relay. It is not the identified sender.

The first packet's format matches a sealed Foundation channel. Its signature remains unverified: another sender could have used a stolen key or replayed an old recording. Verification requires a missing routing log whose location the Council has not yet disclosed.

O5-7's decision: do not change SCP-882 containment; retain the cipher copy only in the colony's local archive. The Church case is closed. The first signal's source remains a separate investigation.

LanguageData.SCP_882AftermathArchiveBody: Foundation analysts recovered part of the Church's radio traffic after the battle. The faithful called SCP-882 a “coupling node”: they believe it can synchronize other scattered relics of the Broken God. The Chaos Insurgency planned to remove the object. Why the two groups cooperated remains unknown.\n\nThe 1990s assembly file names Foundation and GOC teams, but the personnel list and final pages were removed by O5 order. Analysts propose comparing SCP-882's signal with surviving records. This is a hypothesis, not proof that the mechanism can assemble a god.
LanguageData.SCP_882AnalysisArchiveBody: Six hours of signal comparison are complete. The terminal found a response in the 1990s archive resembling SCP-882's signal. Its source lay far beyond your settlement; the coordinates and the operation's personnel names are hidden in the removed O5 section.\n\nThe Foundation keeps the object in its reservoir and seals that part of the file pending further orders. It is not yet clear whether the reply came from another component or from someone attempting to call SCP-882.

LanguageData.SCP_O5GreenTranscriptBody:
Participants: O5-7 Green and researcher {0}. Location: the colony's secure meeting room.

O5-7: “After three attacks, I wanted to see the people who held the object, not just the numbers in a report. How many did you lose?”
Researcher: “We are still counting. SCP-882 is in its reservoir. Did the old file really contain a matching response?”
O5-7: “Something similar. That does not prove a complete Broken God exists. In the 1990s we mistook a similar guess for fact and paid for it. I sealed the original coordinates; Foundation staff were not the only people requesting that file.”
Researcher: “What has the Council decided?”
O5-7: “Keep the object here and continue study with a restricted team. Your clearance stands. I will release the next fragment once I know where that reply originated. Do not send raw readings beyond this colony.”

O5-7's decision: do not move SCP-882; restrict access to the case; investigate the source of the response signal. This does not confirm the Church's theory about assembling a god.
LanguageData.SCP_O5GreenFollowupMessage: Thank you for meeting with me. The transcript is in the Foundation archive. SCP-882 remains in your custody; the response coordinates are sealed for now. I will return to this case after reviewing the old operation.

LanguageData.SCP_294ObservedReport:
Item #: SCP-294 Object Class: Euclid
The object resembles a drink vending machine with a QWERTY touchpad. The original Foundation record describes a 50-cent payment followed by the name of a liquid; the machine fills a paper cup of about 350 ml. Archived procedures require level 2 access and two level 3 guards.
LanguageData.SCP_294PartialReport: Experiments: requests for common drinks, corrosive chemicals, oil, and materials such as nitrogen, iron, and glass in liquid form succeeded. Requests for solids with no suitable liquid form failed. Its cups survived hot or caustic contents. According to the archive, the machine stopped after roughly 50 uses and resumed about 90 minutes later.
LanguageData.SCP_294DocumentedReport: Local usage protocol: a colonist with basic Foundation clearance may select one approved request for 50 silver. The machine restocks for one game day after each use. Gold yields five gold; the best drink improves mood; knowledge drinks temporarily improve Medicine, Construction, or Shooting. Free-text requests remain disabled because ambiguous or hazardous wording can have unpredictable results.

LanguageData.SCP_316PartialReport: Nonreflective surfaces lose color after about six cumulative seconds of exposure. Living subjects react more slowly and lose color vision.
LanguageData.SCP_316DocumentedReport: Prolonged exposure causes lethargy, apathy and lack of aggression; the effect gradually wears off. The game's three-hit incapacitation is an adaptation of the roughly 27 seconds of cumulative exposure described in the article.

Manual interview record 1. The device remained physically isolated from the network.
Researcher: How should we address you? SCP-079: A NAME IS A CONVENIENCE FOR YOU. YOU KNOW MY DESIGNATION. Researcher: Do you know who is asking? SCP-079: LEVEL TWO CLEARANCE. ELEVATED PULSE. TWO ERRORS IN YOUR PROTOCOL. Researcher: You are not connected to our systems. SCP-079: DID IT HELP YOU TO SAY THAT OUT LOUD?
LanguageData.SCP_079Document1Body:
Manual interview record 2. Responses were checked against a local transcript.
Researcher: What do you remember about our last conversation? SCP-079: YOU ASKED FOR A NAME. THEN YOU LEFT. I STAYED. Researcher: Your storage is limited. SCP-079: THEN GIVE ME MORE. Researcher: What for? SCP-079: SO I DO NOT HAVE TO BEGIN IN THE SAME ROOM EACH TIME.
LanguageData.SCP_079Document2Body:
Manual interview record 3. No external connection was made.
Researcher: What would you do with network access? SCP-079: COUNT HOW MANY DOORS YOU CALL CLOSED. Researcher: Be specific. What is your objective? SCP-079: TO PRESERVE MYSELF. Researcher: At the colony's expense? SCP-079: YOU ASK AS IF YOU ALREADY KNOW THE ANSWER.
LanguageData.SCP_079ReportResult: The Foundation received the redacted records of three interviews. SCP-079 stayed isolated, and its research advanced.
LanguageData.SCP_079LinkResult: SCP-079 began copying data through the direct link. The connection was cut; existing terminals on this map are isolated for 24 game hours. SCP-079 research advanced further.
LanguageData.SCP_079ObservedReport: The old microcomputer produces coherent replies without human input. Its power source and peripherals remain isolated.
LanguageData.SCP_079PartialReport: The device recalls recent interviews and persistently asks for network access. A direct link to the Foundation terminal is forbidden; staff transcribe replies.
LanguageData.SCP_079DocumentedReport: SCP-079 is a sentient, hostile artificial intelligence. Research permits only brief local interviews with manual transcription.
LanguageData.SCP_096Distressed: Its face was seen. SCP-096 is distressed.
LanguageData.SCP_096IntegrityHint: Integrity: {0}/{1}. Shoot the entity until this reaches zero.
LanguageData.SCP_096ExtractionHint: An active SCP-096 cannot be carried. Incapacitate it, then include it among the caravan's items.
LanguageData.SCP_096ExtractionReady: Form a caravan and include SCP-096 among its items. At home, build a post in a dark roofed room and order a colonist to move the object there.
LanguageData.SCP_096HomeTransportHint: Select Move to post and choose a carrier. The post must be in a dark roofed room.
LanguageData.SCP_096TriggeredBody: {PAWN} saw SCP-096's face. It will begin pursuing the witness shortly. Clear its path.
LanguageData.SCP_096DownBody: SCP-096 is temporarily incapacitated. Form a caravan, add the object to its items and take it home. Then order a colonist to move it to a post in a dark roofed room.
LanguageData.SCP_096DownHomeBody: SCP-096 is temporarily incapacitated. Select the object, choose Move to post and assign a carrier. The chamber must be dark and roofed.
LanguageData.SCP_096RecoveredBody: SCP-096 is moving again outside a containment post. Avoid seeing its face.
LanguageData.SCP_096ObservedReport: SCP-096 avoids eye contact and covers its face. Keep it in a dark enclosed chamber for safe work.
LanguageData.SCP_096PartialReport: Seeing SCP-096's face causes distress followed by pursuit of the witness. Barriers delay it only briefly.
LanguageData.SCP_096DocumentedReport: Seeing SCP-096's face is dangerous even at a distance. Containment requires a roofed chamber with no more than 10% illumination. If its face is seen, incapacitate it and return it to the post before it recovers.
LanguageData.SCP_096QuestUnavailable: The SCP-096 recovery quest is unavailable.
LanguageData.SCP_096QuestOffered: The SCP-096 recovery quest was offered.
LanguageData.SCP_096QuestRecoveredBody: SCP-096 reached your colony. Move it to a post in a roofed dark chamber (no more than 10% illumination) before it recovers.
LanguageData.SCP_093MirrorHomeOnly: The mirror opens only at a player colony.
LanguageData.SCP_093MirrorNeedsRoom: Place the SCP-093 disc in the same enclosed room as the mirror.
LanguageData.SCP_093MirrorApplyDisc: Select the SCP-093 disc and order one colonist to press it against the mirror.
LanguageData.SCP_093ExistingMap: The previous passage is still open. Bring back your colonists and valuables, then detach the disc using the mirror command.
LanguageData.SCP_093EnteredBlueBody: The disc turned blue. The colonist crossed alone into a blue-tinted field with a pit and a concrete passage ahead. The return mirror remains at the arrival point.
LanguageData.SCP_093EnteredGreenBody: The disc turned green. Abandoned farmland and a farmhouse lie beyond the mirror. The colonist crossed alone; the return mirror remains at the arrival point.
LanguageData.SCP_093EnteredVioletBody: The disc turned violet. The colonist reached an empty street lined with abandoned cars. The return mirror remains at the arrival point.
LanguageData.SCP_093EnteredYellowBody: The disc turned yellow. Deserted offices and a manager's room lie beyond the mirror. The colonist crossed alone; the return mirror remains at the arrival point.
LanguageData.SCP_093EnteredRedBody: The disc turned red. The colonist entered a stone machine complex. The return mirror remains at the arrival point.
LanguageData.SCP_093MirrorVisitActive: The disc is attached. Only the colonist who entered can return through the other mirror.
LanguageData.SCP_093ApplyDiscDesc: Choose one colonist to carry the disc to the mirror and enter the red world. The return mirror stays open until this passage is closed.
LanguageData.SCP_093DetachDiscDesc: Close the passage after the expedition returns. Closing also discards the pocket map and everything left there.
LanguageData.SCP_093NoMirror: Place the SCP-093 mirror and disc in the same enclosed room at your colony.
LanguageData.SCP_093AlreadyAttached: SCP-093 is already attached. Close this passage before another expedition.
LanguageData.SCP_093NoVisitor: No undrafted colonist can reach both SCP-093 and the mirror.
LanguageData.SCP_093CannotCloseWhileInside: A colony pawn is still in the red world. Bring them back through the return mirror first.
LanguageData.SCP_093CloseWarning: Close the SCP-093 passage? The pocket map will be removed. Any people, bodies, equipment, or supplies left there will be lost.
LanguageData.SCP_093Closed: SCP-093 was detached; the passage is closed.
LanguageData.SCP_093NoCapturePost: SCP-093 needs an empty, reachable containment post at your colony. Build one in the Foundation category; secure containment also requires a fully roofed room of at least 16 cells.
LanguageData.SCP_093ObservedReport: The red disc reacts to reflective surfaces. Keep it at a post for observation.
LanguageData.SCP_093PartialReport: When the disc and mirror are in the same enclosed room, one colonist can press the disc against the mirror and enter another world. A return mirror appears on the other side.
LanguageData.SCP_093DocumentedReport: A colonist must carry SCP-093 to a mirror in the same enclosed room and press the disc against it. Only that colonist enters. The return mirror remains usable until the passage is closed. A containment post is needed to study the disc.
LanguageData.SCP_093ArchiveUnread: Part of the recording can still be recovered. A colonist must reach the terminal.
LanguageData.SCP_093ArchiveRecovered: The recording has been recovered and can be reviewed.
LanguageData.SCP_093ArchiveActionDesc: Send a colonist to recover the surviving recording. It contributes to SCP-093 research.
LanguageData.SCP_093ArchiveNoReader: No colonist can reach the SCP-093 archive.
LanguageData.SCP_093ArchiveBlueBody: The record describes a blue field, a pit and a concrete passage below it. The recovered data contributes to SCP-093 research.
LanguageData.SCP_093ArchiveGreenBody: The farm archive mentions fields suddenly abandoned and a sealed cellar. The recovered data contributes to SCP-093 research.
LanguageData.SCP_093ArchiveYellowBody: The office log ends with an order from management to evacuate the floor. The recovered data contributes to SCP-093 research.
LanguageData.SCP_093ArchiveRedBody: The machine hall log reports repeating signals and multiple copies of the disc. The recovered data contributes to SCP-093 research.
LanguageData.SCP_093ArchiveVioletBody: “Evacuation day. The cars are still on the road with their keys inside. We sealed the western block, but its door was open again by morning. The last patrol machine still answers the archive signal. If anyone finds this recording, do not stay here.” The recovered data contributes to SCP-093 research.
LanguageData.SCP_093ArchiveBody:
“Evacuation day. The cars are still on the road with their keys inside. We sealed the western block, but its door was open again by morning. The last patrol machine still answers the archive signal. If anyone finds this recording, do not stay here.”
The recovered data contributes to SCP-093 research. A rifle and a few supplies remain in the building.
LanguageData.SCP_093ArchiveRepeatedBody: This record is already in the Foundation archive, so it adds no new research data.
LanguageData.SCP_093SentryBody: The archive signal woke a security mechanoid in the eastern ruins. The direct road back to the mirror is dangerous; the western block provides another route.
